scope: G4c round 2: an out-of-sample test of the regime law at d = 4. Written AFTER round 1 came back 5/5 at d = 3 and BEFORE any d = 4 measurement of any kind was run. Round 1's file is left untouched on purpose -- amending it would destroy the only thing that makes it evidence.
why_a_second_round: Round 1 hit 5 of 5, which is the point at which a law is least trustworthy and most in need of a test it was not tuned on. Every cell measured so far -- d=2 R=2, d=3 R=3 -- happened to have fibre dimension exactly 1, so 'slope 1' and 'slope d - R + 1' are not yet distinguishable by any data in this repo. d = 4 separates them.

state_of_evidence_when_written.d=1: measured: never rigid at any R (piecewise-linear exemption)
state_of_evidence_when_written.d=2: measured: R=2 slope 1; R=3 saturated at nullity 9; R>=4 rigid, threshold 11 at R=4
state_of_evidence_when_written.d=3: measured: R=3 slope 1; R=4 saturated at nullity 18, extra 12; R>=5 rigid, thresholds 19/14/12 at R=5/6/8

predictions.claim: nullity grows in n with slope 2
predictions.falsified_if: the slope is 1, or is not constant
predictions.basis: THE discriminating prediction of this round. Every measured cell so far had fibre dimension 1, so a law that merely said 'slope 1' would fit all existing data and fail here. If the slope comes back 1, the fibre-dimension formula is wrong and round 1 was pattern-matching.

predictions.claim: nullity grows in n with slope 1
predictions.basis: the same formula at a different (d, R) with the same answer; pairs with P6 to show the slope tracks d - R + 1 rather than d or R alone

predictions.claim: nullity == 30 and extra flexes == 20, constant in n
predictions.falsified_if: nullity is not 30, or varies with n
predictions.basis: the counting law now has two confirmations (9 at d=2 R=3, 18 at d=3 R=4) rather than the one it had in round 1, but it remains a heuristic rather than a derivation

predictions.falsified_if: extra flexes remain positive at every n tested
predictions.basis: the curvature argument, now at its third dimension

predictions.claim: the threshold exceeds both the counting bound (12) and the d = 3, R = 5 threshold (19)
predictions.basis: thresholds at R = d + 2 went 11 (d=2) then 19 (d=3); more parameters per point should keep pushing it up, and the counting bound has been loose in every dimension so far

what_would_count_as_the_law_failing: P6 returning slope 1 -- this would mean the fibre count is not d - R + 1 and round 1's agreement was coincidence
P9 finding no rigid n at all by the top of the scan, with extra flexes still positive
any nullity that is not constant where the law says saturated, or constant where the law says it grows
still_not_claimed: global uniqueness -- everything here is the rank of one Jacobian
D harvested through the instrument from a measured causal set
a written proof; even a perfect scorecard leaves this [MEASURED], not [PROVED]
